To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the choice of IgRT schedule does not affect HRQoL, if the treatment is individually tailored.

the choice of IgRT mode of delivery is not associated with differences in the HRQoIL in CVID patients, if the treatment is individualized after an extensive educational process, and that the HRQoI is significantly impacted by age, and by the presence of minor psychiatric nonpsychiatric disorders.

the health-related quality-of-life of patients with common variable immunodeficiency receiving immunoglobulin replacement therapies by the different routes of administration (subcutaneous, intravenous, and facilitated) is similar, and the choice of the route of administration should be based on the patient’s individual preferences and convenience.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the IgRT mode on HRQoL and not with the impact of CVID on HRQoI.
the quality of life (QOL) in patients with common variable immune deficiency (CVID).

the mode of Ig administration does not impact on the HRQoIL.
the choice of route of administration of IgRT in CVID does not impact the HRoQoL, and that this choice should be based on the individual clinical and practical features of the patient.
the mode of administration does not influence the HRQoI in CVID, but the educational process is a key factor in the choice of IgRT schedule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients receiving IVIG, SC, or fSCIG report a similar HRQoL.
the mode of IgRT administration does not impact the HRQL in patients with CVID, and that the HRQL is mainly influenced by the presence of minor psychiatric nonpsychiatric disorders.
the HRQoI of CVID patients is not influenced by the route of IgRT administration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of an IgRT route should not be based on the HRQoI, but rather on the patient’s clinical and personal characteristics.
patients should be offered a choice of IgRT route and preparation, and that they should not be limited by the availability of the treatment.
the choice of IgRT schedule should not be based solely on HRQoL but on the clinical needs of the patients.
